response.title: Is it okay to leave my fridge plugged into a battery power station all the time so it takes over by itself when the power goes out?
response.answer:
Yes, you can leave your refrigerator plugged into a battery power station 24/7, so it automatically switches to battery power during an outage. However, the power station must support UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) or EPS (Emergency Power Supply) functionality.

Not every portable power station is designed for continuous operation this way.

How it works

Normal operation: wall power supplies the fridge through the station. During an outage, the station switches to battery power.

Five things to check

1. UPS/EPS support: The station should automatically switch to battery when AC power fails. A transfer time under 20–30 ms is generally desirable, but refrigerator compatibility should be tested.

2. Continuous pass-through operation: The manufacturer must explicitly allow the station to remain plugged into the wall while powering appliances indefinitely.

3. Compressor startup power: A fridge might consume 100–250 W while running but briefly require 600–1,500 W or more during compressor startup. The inverter must handle that surge.

4. Battery longevity: Prefer LiFePO4 (LFP) batteries. Even with these, keeping the battery at 100% continuously can accelerate aging. A model with configurable charging limits is useful.

5. Heat and electrical safety: Keep the station ventilated, away from water and refrigerator heat exhaust, and plugged directly into a properly grounded wall outlet. Avoid extension cords and overloaded power strips.

How long would the fridge run?

Here's an illustrative estimate assuming a refrigerator averages 60 W over time, including compressor cycling, and 85% of battery capacity is usable.

60 W

Estimated backup duration

14.5 hours

Approximation only. Actual runtime depends on compressor cycling, inverter idle losses, temperature, and battery condition.

One important distinction

A power station advertised as having pass-through charging doesn't necessarily provide automatic, interruption-free backup. You want one whose manufacturer explicitly supports UPS/EPS operation with continuous AC input and output.

Also, some power stations use battery cycling even when grid power is available, while others bypass the battery. The latter is generally preferable for permanent refrigerator backup.
